page_summary:
The Man in the High Castle is the canonical works record for PKD's novel. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is The Man in the High Castle (1962).

Researchers can use this entry to trace publication context, later commentary, and relationships to other works.

biography_events.event: PKD takes up the I Ching as a working divination and composition tool — the oracle behind The Man in the High Castle.
Putnam publishes The Man in the High Castle, the alternate-history novel written with the I Ching that becomes PKD's breakthrough.
The Man in the High Castle wins the 1963 Hugo Award for Best Novel, PKD's only Hugo.
PKD writes to Ursula Le Guin thanking her for praise of Mr. Tagomi (Man in the High Castle) in her London speech.
In 1981, PKD wrote 33 letters to Russell Galen, turning the correspondence into a sustained discussion of the science-fiction community, religion and theology, and publishing and career pressures.
